title: Count of Matches in Tournament
statement:
A tournament begins with `n` teams and is played in rounds until a single champion is left. Every match is between two teams and exactly one of them moves on.

- If a round starts with an even number of teams `t`, all of them are paired up: `t / 2` matches are played and `t / 2` teams move on.
- If a round starts with an odd number of teams `t`, one team skips the round and moves on automatically while the other `t - 1` are paired up: `(t - 1) / 2` matches are played and `(t - 1) / 2 + 1` teams move on.

Return the total number of matches played over the whole tournament. With `n = 1` no match is needed.
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the rounds works: halve the field each round, add the matches, and handle the odd team that skips ahead. But look at a single match instead of a round. Every match produces exactly one loser, and a loser never plays again. When the tournament ends, every team except the champion has lost exactly once. So the number of matches equals the number of teams that were knocked out, which is `n - 1`, whatever the byes look like.

## Approach

1. Let `teams` be the starting field `n` and `champions` be `1`, the one team that never loses.
2. Every other team is eliminated once: `knockedOut = teams - champions`.
3. Each match removes exactly one team (`lossesPerMatch = 1`), so `matches = knockedOut / lossesPerMatch`.
4. Return `matches`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 7`, so `teams = 7` and `champions = 1`. Six teams must be knocked out, so `knockedOut = 6`, and with one loser per match `matches = 6`. The round-by-round count agrees: `3` matches with 7 teams (one team skips), `2` with 4 teams, `1` with 2 teams, for `3 + 2 + 1 = 6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): one subtraction and one division.
- Space: O(1): a few numbers.

## Pitfalls

- With an odd field, the team that skips the round still counts among the teams moving on: `(t - 1) / 2 + 1`, not `(t - 1) / 2`.
- A simulation that stops at `remaining > 0` instead of `remaining > 1` loops forever on the champion.
- `n = 1` means no match at all, so the answer is `0`, not `1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `teams` | number of teams at the start (`n`) |
| `champions` | teams that never lose: always `1` |
| `knockedOut` | teams that lose exactly once |
| `lossesPerMatch` | teams eliminated by one match: always `1` |
| `matches` | total matches played, the answer |

narration.1: The function receives the number of teams that enter the tournament.
narration.2: Name the starting field so the counting argument reads clearly.
narration.3: Exactly one team, the champion, finishes without a loss.
narration.4: Every other team leaves after its one and only loss.
narration.5: A match always has one winner and one loser, so it removes exactly one team.
narration.6: Dividing the eliminations by the eliminations per match gives the match count, n - 1.
narration.7: Return the count; how the rounds and byes fall never changes it.
